assessments.summary: Measles cases in the US are peaking with a 225% increase in weekly reports over the past 8 months, and news coverage is rising.
Dengue cases in the US are peaking with a 1003% increase in weekly reports over the past 8 months, and news coverage is rising.
Mpox cases in the US are peaking with a 100% increase in weekly reports over the past 8 months, and news coverage is rising.
Polio cases in the US are peaking with a WHO report of circulating vaccine-derived poliovirus type 1 in Syria.
Influenza activity is baseline with a 29% increase in global test positivity and 55% rise in US hospital admissions over the past month.
West Nile virus cases in the US are rising with a 1562% increase in weekly reports over the past 8 months.
Pertussis cases in the US are rising with a 52% increase in weekly reports over the past 8 months.
RSV cases in the US are rising with a 57% increase in hospital admissions over the past month.
US hospital admissions for COVID-19 are at a baseline level with a recent 13% monthly increase, while news coverage has risen significantly.
US reported cases of chikungunya are stable at baseline with a 64% increase over the past 8 months, and Switzerland has reported its first locally acquired cases.
News coverage for norovirus has increased, but Wikipedia readership remains at a low percentile.
Human metapneumovirus activity is rising with a significant increase in news coverage and Wikipedia readership.
Avian influenza (H5N1) cases in the US are stable at baseline, with news coverage and Wikipedia readership showing moderate activity.
US malaria cases are at a baseline level with a recent 13% monthly increase, but the year-to-date count has decreased.
Cholera news coverage is rising, but Wikipedia readership remains at a low percentile.
